summary: Ratified the research report's option (b), stream-encoding-aware ASCII fallback, with one recorded departure: the column budget in bimodal's aligned renderer is derived from the actually-rendered arrow rather than the report's implied hard-coded constant, because a naive '=>' substitution is 1 char WIDER than the Unicode arrow and would overflow the reserved 4-char slot, breaking the alignment the task's hard constraints protect. 8 phases / 9.5h: (1) shared utils/glyphs.py helper with lru_cached encodability probe on getattr(output,'encoding',None); (2) TDD-first cp1252 TextIOWrapper regression coverage that must be RED across all 9 inventoried print sites in 4 theories; (3) route those 9 sites through the helper, including a _to_subscript signature change; (4) derived-width alignment preservation plus an explicit alignment-invariant test (internal consistency per rendering, not cross-rendering equality) covering the latent two-digit-duration overflow; (5) an ADDITIVE PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 leg on test_generate_then_execute reproducing the Windows child-process condition on Linux; (6) progress-bar glyph sweep (decided IN scope, since the block glyphs are the same live crash class; the isatty gate stays out of scope); (7) policy recorded in TESTING_GUIDE.md, bimodal ARCHITECTURE.md, CODE_STANDARDS.md; (8) full-gate run plus an explicit hard-constraint audit. No packaging assertion is weakened, no CI workflow is touched, and PYTHONIOENCODING/PYTHONUTF8 is forbidden in the fixture env as a mitigation.
